items.title: Clem Raymond Interview, 1958-08-25
items.q: Because I heard Oliver play it. He played it, but I never seen it in music before... Oh, no. He came out here with the band.

ctx.x: In Los Angeles, a theater, a diamond.

I don't know if you couldn't read nothing, though. Mm-hmm. Like he spoke about the show. I don't know if you couldn't read nothing. When I just show him, his cause of wine, boy, don't deny my name. That's right. And I'm glad to hear you say that because it's all funny about him being any good reader. He's never no good reader. He criticized his teachers wrongly, too. I was surprised. Yeah, when he made all them trips that got on his feet, composed the numbers. I said, well, he's pretty great. He turned it pretty…
When did you hear Oliver play that? Before you left New Orleans?

items.title: Clem Raymond Interview, 1958-08-25
items.q: Well, I followed the parade true enough, yes, because it's King Oliver, he played and so did Ory. He had a band in Celestan and those are the three bands that mostly got the funeral parades to my knowledge.

ctx.x: Do you remember which bands they were or did you follow any of those musicians? Certain ones that you liked when you were a kid that were your idols you might say and you tried to follow them more?
